extracted.intended_audience: mathematicians and physicists (readers of Newtonian mechanics); scholars studying classical mechanics and geometric/infinitesimal methods
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts and applies geometric and infinitesimal methods to determine bodies' velocities, resistances, and required medium-density distributions for motion along specified curves, under hypotheses about how resistance depends on velocity. Includes algebraic 'moments' rules for generated quantities and series-expansion techniques to recover tangents/curvature from data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodus determinandi curvam ex phaenomenis (method to determine curve and resistance from experiments)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Ilquet methodus determinandl curvam DraF ex phaenomenis quamproxime, & inde colligendl resistentiam & velocitatem quacum corpus projicitur." (Method for determining the curve D r a F from phenomena and thence inferring the resistance and velocity at each place.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure given: project two similar bodies with equal initial speed from D along differing angles; observe landing points F, f; assume a trial ratio of resistance to gravity, represent it by a chosen length S M; compute by calculus the lengths D F, D f for that assumed DP; compare computed D F with experimentally observed D F and plot their difference as perpendiculars M N (positive on one side, negative on the other); draw a smooth curve through points N, N', N'' and the secant to obtain SX which yields the true ratio of resistance to gravity. Iteratively repeat with new assumed ratios to refine the curve and obtain velocities and resistances at singular locations. (Essentially: assume, compute, compare to experiment, record signed differences, fit curve, read off true resistance ratio.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice of resistance law: linear vs quadratic (hypothesis about resistance dependence on velocity)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Caeterum, resistentlam corporum esse in ratione velocitatis, hypothesis est magis mathematica quam naturalis. In mediis, quae rigore omni vacant, resistentiae corporum sunt in duplicata ratione velocitatum." (Resistance proportional to velocity is a more mathematical hypothesis; in rare media resistance is in duplicate (square) ratio of velocities.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance and rationale: choose model according to medium. Linear dependence (resistance ∝ v) is a mathematical hypothesis useful for calculation; in rarer (perfect) media resistance tends to be proportional to v^2 because faster bodies communicate their action to the medium in proportion to the quantity of medium disturbed and time. Note: explicitly state hypothesis before analysis; consequences (e.g., geometric progressions of times/velocities) follow from the chosen law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences and method for quadratic resistance (v^2) — geometric progressions
rubrics_metrics.description: From PROPOSITIO V (THEOREMA III): "Si corpori resistitur in velocitatis ratione duplicata ... tempora vero sumantur in progressione geometrica ... dico quod velocitates initio singulorum temporum sunt in eadem progressione geometrica inverse; & quod spatia sunt aequalia quoe singulis temporibus describuntur."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When modeling motion with resistance ∝ v^2 and taking time-parts in geometric progression, then initial velocities for those time-parts form the inverse geometric progression and the spatial segments described in each time-part are equal. Use geometrical constructions (hyperbolae, areas, ordinates) to represent velocities and spaces; partition time and represent velocities by ordinates so that areas correspond to distances described.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma II: rules for moments of 'generated' (genita) quantities — differential algebra rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition and calculus-rules: 'Genitam voco quantitatem omnem ... Has quantitates ... incrementa vel decrementa momentanea sub nomine momentorum intelligo.' The lemma lists how moments (instantaneous increments) behave under products, powers, contents: e.g., moment of AB is aB + bA, moment of A^n is n a A^(n-1), moment of A^m B^n is m a A^(m-1) B^n + n b A^m B^(n-1), etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prescriptive computational rules for infinitesimal changes ('momenta') used throughout: treat moments linearly, apply product and power rules (essentially differential rules) to compute instantaneous increments of generated quantities. These rules underpin the method of dividing motion into infinitely small parts and composing areas/rectangles to represent space/velocity relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation of motion via geometric areas and ordinates (velocities, times, resistances)
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple propositions instruct representing velocities, times, and resistances by lines, ordinates, areas, and sectors: e.g., velocity by ordinate A P, time by sector or by length along an asymptote, space by area under a curve (area hyperbolica adjacent ABGD), resistances by chosen lines proportional to some function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use geometric correspondences: velocities ↔ ordinates; spaces ↔ areas under hyperbolas or sums of triangular/rectangular elements; times ↔ sectors (circular or hyperbolic) or sums of infinitesimal time-parts. Compose, divide, and compare these geometric objects to deduce relations among physical quantities; when verifying a hypothesis, express the hypothesized ratio as a geometric length and compare computed and experimental areas/lengths.

rubrics_metrics.name: Absolute forces in equal spatial partitions form a geometric progression (Prop. VIII)
rubrics_metrics.description: PROPOSITIO VIII: If a body in uniform medium with uniform gravity ascends or descends and the total space is divided into equal parts, the absolute forces (vis absolutae) at the beginnings of the parts (additively adjusting resistance when ascending or subtracting when descending) form a geometric progression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To deduce force distribution along an assigned path, represent gravity by a fixed line AC, resistance by an indefinite line AK, velocity by mean proportional AP between AK and AC; construct a hyperbola with given asymptotes and partition its area into equal parts. The corresponding absolute forces at those partition points will be in geometric progression. Use this for deducing force variations along equal segments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ascent/descent time as sectors: circular vs hyperbolic (Prop. IX)
rubrics_metrics.description: PROPOSITIO IX: If tangents of sectors of a circle and a hyperbola are taken proportional to velocities (with a fixed radius), then total time of ascent to highest point is proportional to a sector of the circle and total time of descent from the highest point is proportional to a sector of the hyperbola.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Method: construct circle and hyperbola with common center/vertex and use tangent lengths proportional to instantaneous velocities; partition the sectors into infinitesimal elements corresponding to time-particles; sum (integrate) to obtain total times as geometric sector-areas. Use small-part arguments comparing triangle/tangent elements and the corresponding generated velocity/time increments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Problem method for determining medium density for motion on a given curve (Prop. X / Problema III)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given gravity uniform and medium resistance ∝ (density × v^2), determine the medium density at each point so that a body moves along a given curve and determine the body's velocity and the medium resistance at each place.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure: erect ordinates and equal abscissa steps; express times for arc segments as proportional (in subduplicate ratio) to heights the body would reach falling from the tangent (tangent-based construction); express velocity increments as sum of gravitational generated term and negative resistance term; relate these to series expansions of ordinate and tangent lengths (develop ordinates/tangents into convergent series). Solve for density as density ∝ (resistance)/(v^2) using the derived series expressions. Practical solution uses first few terms of the series: first term (infinitesimal) determines tangent length; second term determines the small normal distance between tangent and curve (I N) and thus angular contact; third term determines curvature variation, etc. Example: semicircle gives density proportional to tangent length H T (and resistance ∝ 3·(something) as derived).

rubrics_metrics.name: Series expansion hierarchy guiding interpretation of terms when resolving tangents and curvature
rubrics_metrics.description: When a curve's ordinate (or related quantity) is expanded in a convergent series, terms are classified: the first term corresponds to the infinitesimal leading part (tangent length), the second to the first-dimension variation (distance between tangent and curve determining contact angle), the third to the curvature, the fourth to curvature-variation, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this hierarchy to truncate series when solving practical problems: the first term gives the tangent (direction), the second locates how far the tangent departs from the curve (I N), third/ higher terms refine curvature and higher derivatives. The text advises that in many problems only the first few terms are needed to determine tangents and to approximate medium density or resistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Example rule: semicircle case — density proportional to tangent length
rubrics_metrics.description: Worked example: for PFHQ a semicircle on diameter PQ, expanding and extracting series yields that the medium density at a point H should be proportional to the tangent length H T (with sign conventions when tangent is on opposite side).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute series of ordinate and related terms (P, Q, R, S series), extract leading terms, and substitute into the derived formulae for resistance and density. The semicircle example demonstrates implementing the general procedure; follow algebraic extraction and the method of successive terms as in the worked example.
